One scope mismatch needs alignment:

    Gog succeeds; later file copy fails
      → Preserve files already delivered.

    Gog itself fails midway through a batch
      → Current code exposes none of that command’s files.
      → The specification promises completed-sibling recovery.

I checked pinned Gog: batch JSON arrives only after successful completion. Its atomic file writes might support recovery, but that requires qualifying Gog-specific completion rules—not merely hashing leftover files.

Given your “don’t overengineer” constraint, I recommend shipping the currently qualified single-file commands in v1 and deferring failed-batch recovery. That narrows the written requirement; I haven’t changed it.

I’m pausing at this scope question under discuss-clarify-mental-models: may I defer failed-batch recovery to a follow-up PR?

The [independent review](/private/tmp/agent-oauth-complete-review-2026-09-07.md:1) is complete. We’re not PR-ready: complete-path tests and operational docs remain.

One scope mismatch needs alignment:

    Gog succeeds; later file copy fails
      → Preserve files already delivered.

    Gog itself fails midway through a batch
      → Current code exposes none of that command’s files.
      → The specification promises completed-sibling recovery.

I checked pinned Gog: batch JSON arrives only after successful completion. Its atomic file writes might support recovery, but that requires qualifying Gog-specific completion rules—not merely hashing leftover files.

Given your “don’t overengineer” constraint, I recommend shipping the currently qualified single-file commands in v1 and deferring failed-batch recovery. That narrows the written requirement; I haven’t changed it.

I’m pausing at this scope question under discuss-clarify-mental-models: may I defer failed-batch recovery to a follow-up PR?
